question.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
question.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
question.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

swap.text: This sultan was surprised by Wallachian troops during the Night Attack at Targoviste [ter-GOH-vish-te], after which Vlad impaled 20,000 Turks. This sultan also invaded Serbia and captured Constantinople.
swap.answerHtml: Mehmed II [accept Mehmed the Conqueror; accept “Mehmet” in place of “Mehmed”]
swap.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

question.text: During Timur's conquest of Asia Minor, he defeated and captured the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt near this modern-day capital of Turkey, after which he used Bayezid as a footstool and kept his wife in a cage.
question.clue: Kızılay ] Square, named for a certain "Red Crescent," is in this city, which was once known as Angora.

swap.leadin: ANZAC troops landed at their namesake cove in this battle, and later made another landing at Suvla.
swap.text: Name this World War I battle, also known as the Dardanelles Campaign, that ended in an Ottoman victory over ANZAC forces.
swap.clue: This World War I battle, a disaster planned by Winston Churchill, was fought largely by the ANZAC corps of Australians and New Zealanders. Mustafa Kemal gained fame defending Turkey here.

question.text: This pirate sailed the Barbary Coast with his brother Aruj before becoming an admiral in the Ottoman navy and defeating the Holy League at the Battle of Preveza. He shares his name with a Holy Roman Emperor killed in the Third Crusade.
question.clue: He met with Antonio Rincon to negotiate an alliance between his monarch and Francis I, but his force was defeated at the Battle of Preveza by an allied fleet assembled by Pope Paul III in 1538.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a class of people often found in imperial courts.
swap.text: The Chief Black Eunuch was the guardian of the Ottoman Imperial one of these. Ibrahim the Mad had one, but supposedly drowned all of its members in the Bosporus.
swap.clue: Wives and concubines in Islamic kingdoms were often sequestered in these areas of the palace. They were also called seraglios.

question.leadin: Ipek Calislar ("chah-lish-lahr") was tried for "insulting the memory" of this man after publishing a book that credits Latife Hanım with many of his achievements.
question.text: Name this founder of the Republic of Turkey whose government promoted "Women's Role Models" like beauty pageant winner Feriha Tevfik.
question.answerHtml: Kemal Atatürk [or Mustafa Kemal Pasha; or Mustafa Kemal Ataturk]
question.clue: This leader who successfully defended Gallipoli from invasion and later helped to found a republic, of which he served as the first president.

swap.text: This period of Ottoman reform began with the 1839 "Noble Edict of the Rose Chamber." The reforms of this period, whose name means "reorganization," eliminated millet courts.

question.leadin: Identify these individuals involved in the Gallipoli campaign.
question.text: After Enver Pasha's disastrous defeat at Sarakamis, this German general took control of much of the Ottoman military and oversaw the defense at Gallipoli; he later lost at Megiddo.

swap.leadin: Name these treaties signed or drafted in Switzerland.
swap.text: This 1923 treaty ended the Greek-Turkish war, established a demilitarized zone around the Dardenelles, and transferred Imbros, Tenedos, and part of Thrace.
swap.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

question.text: This man, who had been minister of war at the outbreak of World War I, traveled to Moscow and proposed the idea of overthrowing Kemal with Soviet aid, but was later killed in action against the Red Army during the Basmachi rebellion.
question.clue: As a government minister, this man oversaw the genocidal Special Organization.

swap.leadin: This battle is considered to be the turning point in the Ottoman conquest of Europe.
swap.text: Name this 1529 clash that marked the farthest reach of Ottoman troops into the west. At this battle, Niklas Graf Salm defended a Habsburg city from siege.

question.text: The five smartest children from each of these Ottoman provinces would be selected to learn about vaccines and hajamat blood treatment. The Tanzimat Reforms replaced [emphasize] eyalets ["AY-uh-lets"] with these units, which were led by people like Muhammad Ali in Egypt.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Sevres demilitarized it until 3 years later, when the Treaty of Lausanne gave the rights of this body of water back to Turkey.
swap.text: Name this narrow strait which connects the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea, fought over several times in history.
swap.clue: In 1915 Winston Churchill arranged an attempt by Ian Hamilton to approach the contested site by land from its north.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Ottoman naval exploits from the golden age.
question.text: This was Barbarossa's greatest victory, which came at the expense of the Holy League in 1538.

swap.leadin: One member of this organization wrote the book Three Policies, outlining this group's ideology.
swap.text: Name this organization, also known as the Committee of Union and Progress, which overthrew Sultan Abdul Hamid II.
swap.answerHtml: Young Turks [accept Committee of Union and Progress or CUP before mention; accept Jon Turkler or Genc Turkler; or Les Jeunes Turcs]
swap.clue: This movement was opposed by a secret society called the Savior Officers.

question.text: Many Portuguese Jews reached the Ottoman Empire thanks to the network of this wealthy Sephardic woman, who convinced Suleiman the Magnificent to offer protection to Jews in Ancona. Her nephew received the title Duke of Naxos from Selim II, whom he persuaded to take Cyprus from Venice.

swap.text: Coucy died in captivity after being defeated by Bayezid I at this 1396 battle for a Danubian fortress in Bulgaria. Although John the Fearless had nominal control of French forces at this battle, Coucy called many of the shots.
swap.clue: Stefan Lazarevich's Serbs took part in this battle as vassals of the winning side.

question.leadin: A claim about this event originated in the Annals of the Empire discussing the reign of Holy Roman Emperor Maximilian II.
question.text: Voltaire claimed that "nothing is better known" than what event, where the great commander Dragut was killed by a cannonball while trying to cut off Fort St. Elmo from Fort St. Angelo?
question.clue: This 1565 "Great Siege", during which Knights Hospitallers under the command of Jean de Vallette successfully held off a far superior Ottoman force.

swap.leadin: During this period, the Valide Sultan exerted tremendous power over distribution of public funds, resulting in an increase in public works projects.
swap.text: Name this 130-year period of the Ottoman Empire, during which a succession of child or invalid sultans allowed the Imperial Harem to run the government.
swap.clue: Often considered to begin with the rise in power of Roxelana, a concubine of Sulieman, this period lasting into the 17th century saw the increased influence of the harem and queen regents over Ottoman policy.
